transport_note: Version 1 uses USB serial. Bluetooth serial is the next phase and should reuse the same envelope and backend/frontend flow.

sensors.name: DHT11 Temperature / Humidity
sensors.purpose: Reads ambient temperature and humidity for environmental telemetry.
sensors.wiring_summary: Connect VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and DATA to D22. If you are using a bare DHT11 package instead of a module, add a 10k pull-up resistor from DATA to 5V.
sensors.breadboard_description: Place the DHT11 module at the edge of the breadboard, route power rails first, and keep the data jumper short to reduce noise.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> DHT11 VCC
Mega GND -> DHT11 GND
Mega D22 -> DHT11 DATA

frontend.appearance: Shows temperature and humidity values with numeric history.

constraints: The DHT11 updates slowly; polling faster than about once every 2 seconds will produce stale or invalid reads.
Use a stable 5V supply to avoid checksum errors.

sensors.name: PIR Motion Sensor
sensors.purpose: Detects movement and occupancy changes in front of the sensor.
sensors.wiring_summary: Power the PIR from 5V and GND, then connect OUT to D23.
sensors.breadboard_description: Mount the PIR so the lens points into open space; avoid placing it directly next to motors or the LCD backlight power lines.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> PIR VCC
Mega GND -> PIR GND
Mega D23 -> PIR OUT

frontend.appearance: Shows current motion state and a recent boolean history.

constraints: Most PIR modules need 30 to 60 seconds of warmup after power-on.
The output can remain high for a configurable hold interval depending on the module trimmer.

sensors.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance
sensors.purpose: Measures distance to an object in front of the transducer pair.
sensors.wiring_summary: Connect TRIG to D24 and ECHO to D25. The HC-SR04 runs happily from 5V on a Mega 2560.
sensors.breadboard_description: Place the ultrasonic module off the edge of the breadboard or shield so the transducers face outward with a clear line of sight.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> HC-SR04 VCC
Mega GND -> HC-SR04 GND
Mega D24 -> TRIG
Mega D25 -> ECHO

frontend.appearance: Shows live distance with a sparkline.

constraints: Avoid measuring against soft fabric or angled surfaces if you want stable readings.
Keep the sensor away from fan airflow and strong vibrations.

sensors.name: Sound Sensor Module
sensors.purpose: Reports analog microphone amplitude for ambient noise detection.
sensors.wiring_summary: Use the analog output AO into A0; the digital threshold output is not used in V1 because analog telemetry is more flexible.
sensors.breadboard_description: Keep the module away from the DC motor and fan wiring to reduce electrical noise.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> Sound VCC
Mega GND -> Sound GND
Mega A0  -> Sound AO

frontend.appearance: Shows raw analog level and trend.

constraints: The module output is noisy by nature; treat it as relative intensity instead of calibrated decibels.
Avoid long analog leads.

sensors.name: Rain / Water Sensor
sensors.purpose: Measures water presence using the sensor pad and its controller board.
sensors.wiring_summary: Connect the sensor pad to its driver board, then route AO to A1 and DO to D29 for both raw and thresholded telemetry.
sensors.breadboard_description: Keep the controller on the breadboard but place the sensor pad off-board where it can safely contact water. Dry the pad after testing.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> Rain VCC
Mega GND -> Rain GND
Mega A1  -> Rain AO
Mega D29 -> Rain DO

frontend.appearance: Shows analog rain reading and threshold state.

constraints: Rain pads corrode if left wet for long periods; power them only during tests if you need long life.
Treat the analog value as relative and calibrate thresholds for your module.

sensors.name: Joystick Module
sensors.purpose: Captures X/Y analog position and center-button press state.
sensors.wiring_summary: Connect VRx to A2, VRy to A3, and SW to D26 with the firmware using INPUT_PULLUP on the button line.
sensors.breadboard_description: If your joystick is on a small breakout, seat it near the breadboard edge for easy manual access.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> Joystick VCC
Mega GND -> Joystick GND
Mega A2  -> VRx
Mega A3  -> VRy
Mega D26 -> SW

frontend.appearance: Shows live X/Y axes and button state.

constraints: Raw center values vary slightly by module; expect around 512 at rest, not exactly 512.
Button logic is active-low in this wiring.

sensors.name: Touch Sensor Module
sensors.purpose: Reports capacitive touch contact as a digital input.
sensors.wiring_summary: Power the module from 5V and route SIG to D27.
sensors.breadboard_description: Expose the touch pad so it is easy to press without pulling on the jumper wires.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> Touch VCC
Mega GND -> Touch GND
Mega D27 -> Touch SIG

frontend.appearance: Shows a boolean touch state card.

constraints: Cheap touch modules are sensitive to supply noise and nearby cables.
Mount away from the ultrasonic sensor and RFID antenna when possible.

sensors.name: Rotary Encoder Module
sensors.purpose: Tracks incremental rotation plus the encoder pushbutton.
sensors.wiring_summary: Use D2 and D3 for the quadrature channels and D28 for the pushbutton so rotation can be tracked cleanly.
sensors.breadboard_description: Place the encoder where it can rotate freely without colliding with the USB cable or sensor modules.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega D2  -> Encoder CLK
Mega D3  -> Encoder DT
Mega D28 -> Encoder SW
Mega 5V  -> Encoder +
Mega GND -> Encoder GND

frontend.appearance: Shows current position and recent deltas, with button state.

constraints: Mechanical encoders can bounce; the firmware smooths position at the event level but physical quality still matters.
Keep the channel wires short.

sensors.name: Pushbutton Input
sensors.purpose: Provides a simple digital input and edge-triggered event source.
sensors.wiring_summary: Wire one side of the button to D7 and the opposite side to GND. The internal pull-up keeps the line stable.
sensors.breadboard_description: Straddle the button across the breadboard center gap and verify the legs are on the correct opposing rows.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega D7  -> Button leg 1
Mega GND -> Button leg 2

frontend.appearance: Shows current pressed state and edge events.

constraints: This wiring is active-low.
Do not add an external pull-down at the same time as INPUT_PULLUP.

sensors.name: IR Receiver Module
sensors.purpose: Decodes infrared remote control frames into telemetry events.
sensors.wiring_summary: Connect the IR receiver output to D6 and aim the remote at the receiver while testing.
sensors.breadboard_description: Mount the receiver so the dome faces outward with line-of-sight to the remote.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 5V  -> IR VCC
Mega GND -> IR GND
Mega D6  -> IR OUT

frontend.appearance: Shows the most recent decoded IR code and related events.

constraints: Direct sunlight and some LEDs can interfere with IR reception.
The stored code is the last successfully decoded raw frame in hex.

sensors.name: RC522 RFID / NFC Reader
sensors.purpose: Reads RFID or NFC tag UIDs over SPI and emits scan events.

pins.notes: RC522 must be powered from 3.3V, not 5V.

sensors.wiring_summary: Use 3.3V power only. Connect the module over the Mega hardware SPI pins and use D53 as SS plus D49 for reset.
sensors.breadboard_description: Keep the RC522 antenna face unobstructed and away from noisy motor wiring. Route the SPI wires directly if possible.
sensors.ascii_diagram:
Mega 3.3V -> RC522 VCC
Mega GND  -> RC522 GND
Mega D53  -> SDA/SS
Mega D49  -> RST
Mega D50  -> MISO
Mega D51  -> MOSI
Mega D52  -> SCK

frontend.appearance: Shows the last scanned UID and event log entries for tag scans.

constraints: The RC522 is a 3.3V device. Do not power it from 5V.
Some clones are sensitive to long SPI leads.

sensors.name: 4x4 Matrix Keypad
sensors.purpose: Captures key presses from a 4x4 matrix keypad as telemetry events.
sensors.wiring_summary: Wire the keypad rows to D30-D33 and the columns to D34-D37. The firmware scans the matrix through the Keypad library.
sensors.breadboard_description: The keypad usually plugs directly with jumper wires rather than sitting on the breadboard. Label the ribbon if the connector order is unclear.

frontend.appearance: Shows the last key pressed and event stream entries for each input.

constraints: Matrix keypad pin order differs by vendor; verify the ribbon order before powering up.
The firmware stores only the last key in snapshots, with full key activity preserved as events.
